title: Bitcoin Technical History
description: A comprehensive timeline of Bitcoin's consensus changes, research breakthroughs, and proposed upgrades.
author: Gemini 3.1 Pro

nodes.label: Bitcoin Whitepaper
nodes.subtitle: Satoshi Nakamoto · October 31, 2008
nodes.description: The publication of the Bitcoin whitepaper to a cryptography mailing list, describing a peer-to-peer electronic cash system.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.content: Satoshi Nakamoto solved the double-spending problem using a decentralized peer-to-peer network and a proof-of-work consensus mechanism, laying the groundwork for the first successful decentralized cryptocurrency.

nodes.label: P2SH
nodes.subtitle: BIP 16 · April 1, 2012
nodes.description: Allowed transactions to be sent to a script hash (address starting with '3') instead of directly to a public key or standard script.

sections.heading: Key Innovations
items: Moved the burden of providing the conditions to redeem coins to the receiver
Allowed complex scripts without bloating the UTXO set until spent

nodes.label: BIP 34
nodes.subtitle: BIP 34 · March 24, 2013
nodes.description: Required blocks to include their block height in the coinbase transaction.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.content: Before BIP 34, it was possible to create identical coinbase transactions for different blocks, leading to the risk of duplicated transaction IDs (txids). By mandating the block height inside the coinbase, every coinbase transaction became globally unique.

nodes.label: BIP 66
nodes.subtitle: BIP 66 · July 4, 2015
nodes.description: Required ECDSA signatures to follow strict Distinguished Encoding Rules (DER).

sections.heading: Overview
sections.content: Restricted OpenSSL's liberal parsing of signatures to a strict standard, reducing a vector for transaction malleability.

nodes.label: CLTV
nodes.subtitle: BIP 65 · December 15, 2015
nodes.description: Introduced an absolute timelock at the script level.

sections.heading: Key Innovations
items: Allowed outputs to be locked until a specific block height or UNIX timestamp
Crucial building block for payment channels and the Lightning Network

nodes.label: CSV
nodes.subtitle: BIP 112 · July 4, 2016
nodes.description: Introduced a relative timelock at the script level.

sections.heading: Key Innovations
items: Allowed outputs to be locked for a specific amount of time AFTER they are confirmed
Made Lightning Network channels capable of remaining open indefinitely

nodes.label: SegWit
nodes.subtitle: Pieter Wuille et al. · August 24, 2017
nodes.description: Segregated Witness (SegWit) fundamentally changed how transaction data is structured by separating the unlocking signatures (witness) from the transaction data.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.content: By moving signature data to an appended structure, SegWit effectively increased the block size limit without a hard fork and fixed third-party transaction malleability.

sections.heading: Key Innovations
items: Introduced block weight (up to 4 million weight units)
Enabled easier integration of layer-2 solutions like Lightning Network
Paved the way for future script upgrades via script versioning

nodes.label: Lightning Network
nodes.description: A decentralized network using smart contract functionality in the blockchain to enable instant payments across a network of participants.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.content: The Lightning Network allows participants to open payment channels with each other, transacting instantly and with near-zero fees by keeping the majority of transactions off-chain, settling on the Bitcoin blockchain only when necessary.

sections.heading: Dependencies
sections.content: Lightning relies heavily on CLTV and CSV for its channel mechanics, and SegWit to fix transaction malleability which previously made channels unstable.

nodes.label: Schnorr Signatures
nodes.description: An elegant signature scheme offering linearity, making multisig look like a single signature.

nodes.label: DLCs
nodes.description: A system for creating private, scalable smart contracts on Bitcoin based on oracle attestations.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.content: DLCs allow two parties to create a smart contract on Bitcoin that resolves based on the signature of an external oracle, without the blockchain or the oracle knowing the details of the contract.

nodes.label: Taproot
nodes.subtitle: BIP 341 · November 14, 2021
nodes.description: A major upgrade integrating Schnorr signatures and Merklized Alternative Script Trees (MAST) to improve privacy, efficiency, and smart contract flexibility.

sections.heading: Key Innovations
items: Indistinguishability of complex scripts from standard single-sig spends

nodes.label: BitVM
nodes.description: A paradigm to express Turing-complete smart contracts on Bitcoin without changing consensus rules.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.content: BitVM operates on a verification model similar to Optimistic Rollups. Computations are done off-chain, and only the verification of fraud proofs happens on-chain via a complex challenge-response game utilizing Taproot trees.

nodes.label: Ark
nodes.description: A layer-2 protocol offering scalable off-chain payments without requiring users to manage channel liquidity.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.content: Ark relies on an untrusted intermediary (Ark Service Provider) who coordinates transactions into a single on-chain footprint. Users can transact asynchronously, making onboarding easier than Lightning.

nodes.label: APO
nodes.description: A proposed signature hash type that allows a signature to commit to a transaction without specifying exactly which inputs are being spent.

sections.heading: Key Benefits
sections.content: Crucial for Eltoo, an alternative Lightning Network channel design that dramatically simplifies state management and removes the risk of toxic channel state penalties.

nodes.label: CTV
nodes.description: A proposed opcode to introduce basic covenants to Bitcoin.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.content: CTV allows a transaction to restrict the ways in which its outputs can be spent in the future by committing to a specific hash of the spending transaction's outputs.

sections.heading: Use Cases
items: Congestion control (batching transactions to save fees)

nodes.label: OP_CAT
nodes.description: A proposal to re-enable OP_CAT, an original Bitcoin opcode removed by Satoshi.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.content: OP_CAT takes two items from the stack and pushes their concatenation. Combined with Schnorr signatures, it enables powerful covenants and the verification of zero-knowledge proofs directly on Bitcoin.
